newsitem.title: INDIA: Creeping doubts seen limiting India stocks rally.
newsitem.headline: Creeping doubts seen limiting India stocks rally.

text.p: Indian shares, which surged nearly four percent early this week, paused on Tuesday on scattered profit-taking and doubts that promised government steps to boost capital markets would match expectations, dealers said.

"The market is slowly discounting the announcements... perhaps there is a feeling that major government measures would be pushed to the budget," said R. Ramakrishnan, chief dealer at ASK-Raymond James Securities India Ltd.

"I think perhaps the market expectations might have been overplayed a bit...but there is likely to be a lot volatility till the budget announcements," said Motilal Oswal, member- broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
Analysts said the market expected the government to allow companies to buy back their shares, reducing equity overhang, and to scrap taxes on shareholders' dividends.
In afternoon trade, the Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark 30-share index was down 15.25 points, or 0.43 percent, after dithering in a 23-point range.
The Bombay index jumped 127 points, or 3.75 percent, in hectic trade on Monday as speculators built up positions in frontline stocks.
"The fact that a certain amount of selling has been absorbed is indicative of the market strength," said Neeraj Roy, head of institutional sales at Prime Broking.
The benchmark BSE index has risen by nearly 16 percent this year on widespread expectations of government steps to bolster the markets.
"Basically, local buying has (been) stepped up...we have seen some kind of movement in the broader market," said Yogendra Shah, director of brokers YSN Shares Pvt Ltd.
But this year's rally has come on the back of wild index swings with increased speculative bidding in top stocks prompting investors to stay clear of volatile markets.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Monday said the government would announce new economic policy measures this week before he and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram leave to attend the World Economic Forum in Davos on January 31.
"Some decisions will be coming in the next two to three days," Deve Gowda told a business gathering in Bombay.
Parliament's approval will be needed for further measures the government planned to announce in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget set for February 28, he said.
Widespread speculation about government policies was expected to keep prices in positive territory, analysts said.
